title: ownerOrNotGriefed guard is bypassed by calling stake/unstake/claim, which invoke _syncBudget directly and can dilute the reward rate
description:
The `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier (lines 114-121) was added to `topUp` and `pullAndRefresh` to mitigate prior finding ES-01 (rate-dilution grief via permissionless window reset). However, the dilution mechanism lives inside `_syncBudget` (lines 208-220), which is invoked from THREE additional entrypoints that DO NOT carry the guard:

- `stake()` at line 248 — `_syncBudget()` runs before any stake-amount checks.
- `unstake()` at line 268 — `_syncBudget()` runs before debt/principal updates.
- `claim()` at line 282 — `_syncBudget()` runs unconditionally, even for callers with zero stake.

Since `claim()` has no requirement that `msg.sender` holds any stake (`user.amount == 0` just yields `pending == 0` and the function no-ops), an attacker with zero stake can spam `claim()` to trigger `_syncBudget`, which in turn calls `dispatcherHook.pull()` and — on any non-zero inflow — unconditionally resets `windowEnd = block.timestamp + windowDuration` and `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. This is the exact attack described in ES-01, now resurfacing via the unguarded path.

The arithmetic is identical to ES-01: with `t` seconds elapsed since the last reset, the post-`_updatePool` budget is `B*(1 - t/D)` (approximately); a small inflow `ε` makes the new rate `(B*(1 - t/D) + ε) / D`, which is strictly less than the old rate `B/D` whenever `t > 0` and `ε << B*t/D`. The net effect is a permanent, permissionless rate reduction for legitimate stakers, executable as often as the dispatcher accrues any mint-debt.

The entry cost is slightly higher than pre-fix: an attacker now pays gas for a `claim()` call instead of `pullAndRefresh()`, but the vector is otherwise identical. `stake(1)` and `unstake(1)` offer additional entry points for attackers who hold a single ERC1155 unit.
impact: Rate-dilution grief against legitimate stakers, permissionlessly and at low cost, identical in outcome to prior ES-01. Each call extends `windowEnd` to `now + windowDuration` and floor-recomputes the rate against the slightly-drawn-down budget, compounding the dilution over repeated calls. Long-term stakers systematically under-earn; the back-loaded residue accrues to whoever stakes late, redistributing value from patient holders to opportunistic ones.
proof:
1. Deploy the staker with any reasonable initial budget and `windowDuration = DEFAULT_WINDOW = 540 days`.
2. After any elapsed time, the dispatcher has accrued some mint-debt. (Per the prior ES-01 analysis, this happens on essentially every block.)
3. Attacker (with no stake) calls `claim()`. `_syncBudget` runs, sees non-zero inflow, and resets `windowEnd = now + 540 days` and `rewardRate = rewardBudget / 46,656,000`. The `claim` body proceeds with `pending = 0` and no payout — but the state mutation from `_syncBudget` has already taken effect.
4. Repeat on every block (or every time dispatcher has accrued meaningful mint-debt). Each call further back-loads the schedule.
5. Legitimate stakers see their effective rate collapse toward `budget / windowDuration` asymptotically, instead of the originally-promised rate.
suggested-fix:
Apply the `ownerOrNotGriefed` guard (or an equivalent guard) to every public/external function that triggers `_syncBudget`, i.e. also to `stake`, `unstake`, and `claim`. Note that these functions already call `_syncBudget` themselves, so the modifier's pre/post snapshot semantics will still work correctly. Simplest: move the guard INSIDE `_syncBudget` itself (capture `rPre/endPre` at entry, require post-condition at exit), gated by `msg.sender != owner()`. That makes the protection intrinsic to the dilution path and closes the bypass in one place.

Alternative: remove the unconditional window reset from `_syncBudget` (amortize inflow into the remaining window instead of resetting to a fresh full window), which removes the grief vector at its root rather than gating it behind a caller check.
